benchmark: VESC BMS -> S6: CAN bitmap vs validity chain, CRC15/PEC silent failure, permission/derating chain (independent)

upstream_ref.note: Independent teaching implementation / counterexample; no GPL code copied. PEC is a generic CRC-15 (poly 0x4599, seed 0x2B0), not asserted byte-identical to the upstream PEC variant.

can_bitmap.note: Pack/unpack is mechanical and accepts any 8-bit node; the upper validity chain separately enforces node range, command set and sample freshness. status bit2=charge_allowed, bit3=charge_ok (VESC-02). Cache reclaim (10 min) is distinct from safety freshness (10 s) (VESC-03).

pec.note: Independently authored CRC-15 detects 1-bit, 2-bit and adjacent burst flips. With the comparison disabled (upstream open-wire block commented out, VESC-07) the identical corruption is accepted without any check -- a silent failure registered as counterexample.

permission_derating.note: Authorization (permission bitmap) and derating (parameter clamp) are separate decisions and independently testable; an unauthorized write is denied+logged, while an authorized command under a derating flag is executed with its charge current clamped 2500->1000 mA.
